title: What does hesed mean?
summary: Hesed is commonly rendered with words such as steadfast love, loyal kindness, or faithful mercy; no single English phrase captures every setting. Exodus 34 uses it in describing God’s character, Ruth 1 shows it through care between people, and Psalm 136 turns it into a repeated line of praise. The surrounding passage helps readers see what this enduring commitment looks like in practice.
historical_context: The cited passages use hesed in more than one relationship. Exodus 34:6–7 describes it as part of God’s character; Ruth 1:8–17 portrays Naomi speaking of kindness and loyalty within a family relationship; the Psalms praise God’s enduring commitment; and Hosea 2 connects it with restoration. These contexts show why a reader should ask who is acting toward whom before choosing an English gloss.
ancient_near_east_context: The recorded examples show hesed in Scripture as both divine commitment and human care: Exodus 34 and Psalm 136 speak of God, while Ruth 1 depicts loyalty between people. Those passages supply enough context to understand the word’s role here; the source list does not include comparative treaty evidence, so no broader treaty claim is needed.
literary_context: The word appears in different literary settings. Exodus 34 places it in a description of God’s character; Psalm 136 repeats that God’s hesed endures throughout a retelling of divine acts; Ruth 1 uses the language of kindness in a family crisis; and Hosea 2 places it in a promise of renewed relationship. The pattern is not one fixed formula: each passage shows commitment through its own story or poem.
covenantal_significance: Hesed helps describe the commitment that sustains relationship through difficulty. In Exodus 34 and Psalm 136 it grounds praise of God; in Ruth 1 it is visible in care for another person; in Hosea 2 it accompanies restoration. The word therefore connects covenant faithfulness with concrete acts of mercy and loyalty, rather than naming only an inward feeling.
canonical_role: This question invites readers to follow hesed across narrative, worship, and prophecy. The passages show God’s character, human loyalty, communal praise, and restoration, while Micah 6:8 places loving hesed among the practices God requires. Comparing those settings helps readers see the word’s range without assuming one English gloss will work everywhere.

interpretive_notes.note: Do not force one English gloss into every occurrence: these passages use hesed in descriptions of God, human loyalty, praise, and restoration.
God's hesed shapes both his saving action and his people's character.
